summary: Finalization delay in structured-output JSON mode causing multi-second tail latency and request timeouts for streaming responses
description:
Issue summary: Customers observed long-tail latency only in structured-output (JSON) mode when responses are streamed. The majority of tokens stream quickly, but the finalization step that validates/normalizes optional JSON fields delays the final bytes and can trigger client-side request timeouts.

Impact: PixlDocs (dedicated customer) reports 0.5-3s extra tail latency on ~8% of streaming calls, causing intermittent client timeouts and degraded UX for their document generation workflow.

Environment: prod us-east-1, dedicated pool assigned to PixlDocs. Observed across redwood-instruct-v1 and a pinned llama-3-13b-8bit replica.

Observed behaviour: streaming SSE frames arrive normally then final SSE chunk stalls; server logs show decoder CPU spike and a blocking call in "json_finalizer::wait_for_optional_field" before emitting EOS.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create streaming chat completion request with format: 'output: JSON {title:string, tags?: [string], metadata?: object}'
2) Use payloads where tags/metadata are often omitted (optional fields) and enable strict_json=true
3) Send at production token rate against dedicated pool (PixlDocs config)
4) Observe client-side timeout or delayed final SSE chunk in ~5-10% of requests
5) Reproduce reliably by toggling strict_json on/off and using same prompt set
logs: 2026-03-10T13:14:22Z request_id=ce4b1f: token_stream OK until finalization; finalizer entered; cpu=86% on decoder-core-2; wall_time_delta=2.9s
2026-03-10T13:15:07Z request_id=d9a2bc: SSE frames last frame delayed by 1700ms; client reported timeout after 1200ms; server emitted EOS at +2.1s
Trace excerpt: json_finalizer.cpp:line 214 wait_for_termination_if_optional() blocking on condvar; caller stack: decode_chunk -> try_emit -> finalize_optional_field
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: strict_json finalization path waits for a separator or EOF token that occasionally doesn't arrive until decoder finishes background normalization work.
Reproduced internally by toggling strict_json and replaying PixlDocs prompt set — tail latency reproduces only with strict_json=true and when optional fields are omitted.

Profiling shows decoder thread executes a synchronous normalization routine that scans entire KV cache for optional keys and acquires a global mutex. Contention observed when multiple concurrent streaming requests hit the same model replica.
Perf dashboard: https://internal.redwood/perf/dashboards/tail-latency?env=prod&customer=PixlDocs - shows 95p->99p jump aligned with times of heavy concurrent streams.

Triage notes: Not a kernel issue nor hardware OOM; CPU and mutex contention in the finalizer path is primary cause. Candidate fixes: async finalization, reduce global mutex scope, short-circuit when optional fields absent, or provide runtime flag to skip strict validation for streaming.

resolution_notes: Mitigation: Released hotfix that short-circuits strict JSON finalization for streaming requests when optional fields are absent; exposed as feature flag 'decoder.skip_strict_json_in_streaming'. Rollout staged: 20% -> 50% -> 100% on PixlDocs dedicated pool.
Workaround given to customer: set allow_incomplete_json=true in SDK or reduce concurrent streams per replica to <= 16.

Root cause: synchronous normalization routine holding global decoder mutex when scanning KV cache for optional fields during strict finalization path; under high concurrency this produced tail blocking.
Permanent fix plan: refactor json_finalizer to use per-request state and async normalization in PR #4123. Follow-up internal refactor ticket INT-33421 created for broader correctness/lock removal.
Post-incident: alert rule added for >500ms finalization_count bucket; playbook updated with runbook steps and the new FF name.
